experiments.title: One LinkedIn carousel a week instead of one text post
experiments.hypothesis: We believe that publishing one carousel a week on the company page will raise weekly LinkedIn impressions because the weekly text posts of the last four weeks stayed flat and a carousel keeps readers on the post for several slides.
experiments.change: Publish one carousel built with carousel-builder on Tuesday morning, in place of the weekly text post.

readout.reason: a change of the weekly mean beyond the band reads in 1 week(s)

experiments.title: Newsletter box at the end of every blog article
experiments.hypothesis: We believe that a newsletter box at the end of each article will raise weekly signups because readers who finish an article have no next step today.
experiments.change: Add the signup box under the last paragraph of every article, same copy everywhere.

readout.reason: the target sits inside the noise of 2 week(s): lengthen it, pick a bigger lever or a metric with more volume

experiments.title: Invite link in the application confirmation email
experiments.hypothesis: We believe that an invite link in the confirmation email will bring referred applicants because applicants often apply with a cofounder or a friend in mind.
experiments.change: Add a personal invite link to the confirmation email and track the signups that come through it.

readout.reason: metric to instrument first: no baseline to read against

usage: Input of the next sprint. Each experiment is a hypothesis to test, never a finding: run it as written, record the start date, let the next growth-pulse run judge it from its metric. Spending needs the founder's approval first (spend_requires_approval).
